date_label: Met 1915; companions for the rest of Barney's life
summary: Barney and Brooks met in 1915 and remained attached for the rest of Barney's life, on terms Brooks set: Souhami records that she did not want a sustained one-to-one relationship, and found Barney's other affairs hard to endure. Barney's own words for her survive - 'I love my Angel better than anything else in the world and prove it.'

sources.quote: They schmoozed together and called it 'dancey prancey'. Romaine was Angel, or Angel Birdie, Natalie was Nat Nat. They were 'Darling' to each other. When they met, in 1915, Romaine was forty-one, Natalie thirty-nine.
sources.context: The opening of Souhami's chapter 22, 'Natalie and Romaine'.
sources.supports: The dated meeting, the ages as the page states them, and the names they used for each other.
sources.provenance: PDF page 171; printed folio 137 confirmed on the rendered page image.

sources.quote: I love my Angel better than anything else in the world and prove it.
sources.context: Barney on Brooks, quoted by Souhami on the same page, in a passage reporting that she told Brooks she was beautiful and a genius and that Brooks was 'dearer to her than her own life'. 'Angel' is Barney's name for Brooks.
sources.speaker: Natalie Clifford Barney
sources.supports: Barney's own declaration of love for Brooks - the participant testimony this connection's class rests on.
sources.provenance: PDF page 171; printed folio 137 confirmed on the rendered page image. The sentence is printed inside Souhami's narration and is quoted here alone, so that what stands as the quotation is entirely in Barney's voice.
